Vijaysen Reddy Bench: Raghvendra Singh Chauhan, B.Vijaysen Reddy High Court For The State Of Telangana The Hon'Ble The Chief Justice Raghvendra Singh Chauhan And The Hon'Ble Sri Justice B. Vijaysen Reddy Writ Petition No.13996 of 2020 Date: 29.12.2020 Between Abdul Basheer. ... Petitioner And The State of Telangana, Rep. by its Principal Secretary, General Administration (Spl. (Law & Order) Department, Secretariat, Hyderabad and others. ...Respondents Counsel for the petitioner : Mr. Pasham Trivikram Reddy Counsel for the respondents : Mr. T. Srikanth Reddy Gp for Home The Court made the following: 2 Order:
texts.facts: and despite opposition, he was granted bail on 17.12.2019. Subsequently, the detenu admitted guilt before the Jail Adalath. 5. Cr.No.222 Bahadurpura u/s 392 24.10.2019 Detenu moved bail petition of 2019 PS vide CRLPMP.No.2155 of IPC in Dt.20.10.19 2019 before Sp. JFCM, Cr.No.319 Hyderabad and despite of 2020 opposition, he was granted conditional bail on 17.12.2019. However, the detenu continues to be in judicial custody as he has not furnished sureties. 6. The detenu was granted bail in four criminal cases, out of which in three cases he was granted conditional bails. However, the detenu was not released on bail since he did not furnish sureties in all the four criminal cases. The detaining authority strongly believed that after release of the detenu on bail, upon furnishing sureties, there is imminent possibility of the detenu indulging in similar activities. The grant of bail is regulated under the provisions of Cr.P.C. Every accused has a right to apply for bail and the concerned Court grants bail taking into consideration various factors. There is a structured mechanism available under the provisions of Cr.P.C. Having availed statutory mechanism, the detenu applied for bail and he was granted bail. As seen from the record, bails are Abdul Basheer vs The State Of Telangana And 2 Others on 29 December, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168023320/ 3 conditional bails and in such case, even if the detenu is released on bail, upon furnishing sureties, he will be subjected to the conditions of bail.
texts.arguments: In a recent decision of this Court in RAPOLU MAHALAKSHMI v. STATE OF TELANGANA1 it was held as under: "12. Every violation of criminal law does cause a rippled in the society. But the ripples can be calmed down by use of normal 2019 (2) ALD (Crl.) 950 (TS) Criminal Justice System. It is only when an offence strikes the society, like a tsunami, that as a weapon of the last resort, the detaining authority is justified in invoking the powers under preventive detention laws. The detaining authority should also examine whether the release of the detenu can be prevented by opposing his bail applications or not? Whether his detention under judicial custody can be ensured or not? In SHASHI AGARWAL v. STATE OF UP2 case t was held as under: (1998) 1 SCC 436 "Every citizen in this country has the right to have recourse to law. He has the right to move the court for bail when he is arrested under the ordinary law of the land. If the State thinks that he does not deserve bail the State could oppose the grant of bail. The possibility of the court granting bail may not be sufficient. There must also be credible information or cogent reasons Abdul Basheer vs The State Of Telangana And 2 Others on 29 December, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168023320/ 4 apparent on the record that the detenu, if enlarged on bail, would act prejudicially to the interest of public order." 8. In order to invoke the provisions of the preventive detention laws, it is necessary for the detaining authority to pass order of detention only when the activities of the detenu are prejudicial to the maintenance of public order. Law and order and public order are two different concepts. The distinction between law and order and public order is succinctly laid in PUSHKAR MUKHERJEE v. STATE OF WEST BENGAL3, the Supreme Court held as under: "The question to be considered in the present case is whether grounds (a), (b) and (e) served on Subhas Chandra Bose are grounds which are relevant to "the maintenance of public order". All these grounds relate to cases of assault on solitary individuals either by knife or by using crackers and it is difficult to accept the contention of the respondent that these grounds have any relevance or proximate connection with the maintenance of public order. Does the expression "public order" take in every kind of infraction of order or only some categories thereof. When two people quarrel and fight and assault each other inside a house (1969) 1 SCC 10 or in a street, it may be said that there is disorder but not public disorder. The contravention of any law always affects order but before it can be said to affect public order, it must affect the community or the public at large. A mere disturbance of law and order leading to disorder is thus not necessarily sufficient for action under the Preventive Detention Act but a disturbance which will affect public order comes within the scope of the Act." Abdul Basheer vs The State Of Telangana And 2 Others on 29 December, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168023320/ 5 The learned author has pointed out that out of 331 indictable English offences 203 are public wrongs and 128 private wrongs." 9. The High Court of Judicature for the State of Telangana and the State of Andhra Pradesh in C. NEELA v. STATE OF TELANGNA4 held as under: "...The State cannot find an easy way out by choosing to invoke the draconian provisions of preventive detention laws against every criminal as a substitute for his prosecution. As discussed supra, the Supreme Court has drawn a clear distinction between disturbance to public order on one side and disturbance to law and order on the other and held that only in the former case the State is permitted to invoke the powers under the preventive detention laws." 10.
